boxes.question: Does the piece read as a personal manifesto expressing the writer’s identity and aesthetic?
Does it clearly present vintage remake fashion as a way to rebel against fast fashion?
Does it give the writer’s clothes a battle-armor-like meaning?
Does it describe distinctive clothing details, such as patches or stitches, as part of the writer’s aesthetic?
Does it portray those clothes or details as resisting standardized industrial aesthetics?
Does the piece maintain a proud, slightly defiant tone that conveys the attitude “I define my own aesthetic”?
Is the writing coherent and engaging enough to work as a polished manifesto?
